problem: An arithmetic series has the first term ${a}_{1}=-3,$ the second term is ${a}_{2}=0,$ and the sum of the series is ${S}_{N}=27.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.

feedback.problem: An arithmetic series has the first term ${a}_{1}=-1$ the $6$th term ${a}_{6}=1.5,$ and the sum of the series is ${S}_{N}=6.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.
feedback.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series.

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)
$$

Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{6}-{a}_{1}}{6-1} \\  & =\frac{1.5-(-1)}{5} \\  & =\frac{2.5}{5} \\  & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting ${a}_{1}=-1$, $d=0.5$, and ${S}_{N}=6$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 6 & =\frac{N}{2}(2\cdot (-1)+(N-1)\cdot 0.5) \\ 12 & =N(-2+0.5N-0.5) \\ 12 & =N(0.5N-2.5) \\ 12 & =0.5{N}^{2}-2.5N \\ 24 & ={N}^{2}-5N\end{aligned}
$$

Factoring the above equation, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{N}^{2}-5N-24 & =0 \\ (N-8)(N+3) & =0 \\ N & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we take the positive solution because $N$ can't be negative.
